title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Lanthanide contraction, combined with a rigid peptide pocket and hydrophobic self-assembly, can amplify small ionic-radius differences into selective aggregation and rare-earth separation.
explanation: Hydrophobic sequences create a low-polarity confined microenvironment that raises affinity for target ions. The rigid LBTLLA3− pocket is described as recognizing Ln3+ of a matching radius, forming negatively charged complexes that assemble into micrometer aggregates and cascade-amplify separation selectivity.
scope: Peptide-based lanthanide recognition and separation, specifically the LBTLLA system.
conditions: Rigid peptide pocket, hydrophobic and electrostatic assembly into micrometer-scale aggregates.
caveats: Presented as a designed example based on lanthanide contraction, not a universal separation process for every ligand class.
